title: Funding Affordable Homes & Home Repairs in Austin
summary:
*   Nearly $600,000 in federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds were reallocated from new homeownership development to support critical homeowner rehabilitation programs.
*   Approved a forgivable loan of up to $185,000 for Austin Habitat for Humanity to acquire land and build 11 affordable single-family homes in the Montopolis neighborhood for low and moderate-income first-time buyers.

AUSTIN HOUSING FINANCE CORPORATION
SPECIAL CALLED MEETING MINUTES
THURSDAY, APRIL 24,2003
The Board of Directors of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) was convened on
Thursday, April 24, 2003, in the Hancock Building Board Room of the Lower Colorado River
Authority, 3700 Lake Austin Blvd. The following were the AHFC items considered by the Austin
Housing Finance Corporation's Board of Directors.
Vice President Goodman called the meeting to order at 3:02 p.m.
AHFC- 1 
Approve the minutes of the March 27, 2003 Board meeting of the Austin Housing
Finance Corporation.
The minutes for the Austin Housing Finance Corporation Special Called Meeting of
March 27, 2003 were approved on Board Member Slusher's motion, Board
Member Alvarez' second on a 6-0 vote. President Garcia was absent.
AHFC- 2 
Amend the Austin Housing Finance Corporation 2002-2003 budget and the service
agreement with the City of Austin to reprogram $585,000 of Community Development
Block Grant (CDBG) funds from the Homeownership Development Program to the
Homeowner Rehabilitation Program. (Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
funds are available from the Acquisition and Development Program.)
(Recommendations made by the Community Development Commission (CDC) on
proposed amendments.) (Related Item 15)
The motion authorizing the amendment of the 2002-2003 budget and the service
agreement was approved on Board Member Dunkcrley's motion, Board Member
Thomas' second on a 6-0 vote. President Garcia was absent.
AHFC- 3 
Approve the negotiation and execution of a Community Housing Development
Organization (CHDO) program forgivable HOME loan, in an amount not to exceed
$185,000, to Austin Habitat for Humanity (AHFH) for the acquisition and development
of a single tract of land into eleven lots in the Montopolis neighborhood. AHFH will
construct 11 affordable single-family homes on the lots for low and moderate-income
first-time homebuycrs. (Funding is available in HOME grant funds allocated in the fiscal
year 2002-2003 Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) budget.)
The motion authorizing the negotiation and execution of a Community Housing
Development Organization program forgivable HOME loan was approved on
Board Member Thomas' motion, Board Member Dunkerlcy's second on a 6-0 vote.
President Garcia was absent.
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 3:08 p.m. was approved on Board Member Dunkcrley's
motion, Board Member Wynn's second on a 6-0 vote. President Garcia was absent.
